note: The fuzzer input bytes are copied into a DataBuf and opened as an Exiv2 image.
After metadata parsing and structure printing, the harness rewrites metadata for the same input image.
The input reaches the JPEG rewrite pass with APP13 segments present.
An APP13 segment is recognized as Photoshop data because its segment payload contains the Photoshop 3.0 signature.
The Photoshop IRB bytes after the signature are appended to psBlob; append reserves extra vector capacity beyond the logical size.

code: DataBuf newPsData = Photoshop::setIptcIrb(!psBlob.empty() ? psBlob.data() : nullptr, psBlob.size(), iptcData_);
note: The accumulated Photoshop data is handed to setIptcIrb for IPTC block replacement during metadata writing.
The loop calls locateIptcIrb with pPsData plus the current offset and computes the remaining length using unchecked unsigned subtraction.
A malformed odd-sized IPTC IRB makes the padding term advance pos past the logical end of psBlob.
The wrapped remaining length lets locateIrb continue with a pointer beyond the vector logical size.
memcmp reads four bytes from the out-of-bounds pointer, producing the reported ASAN container-overflow.
